finding: The test's happy-path branch fires a REAL execute_command with a valid flavor at a sandbox-ENABLED server and accepts the SSE branch, which tokio::spawns run_execute BEFORE responding; require_download_consent is false in the harness, so it reaches ensure_pin_initialized (api.github.com) and can start a 57 MB / 853 MB GitHub Releases download that dropping the response does not cancel. A test documented as proving the refusal lands before any network call is itself network-dependent.
The same happy-path block is also vacuous as a control: it `continue`s on SSE and otherwise only asserts !contains("must be one of"), so deleting resolve_execute_flavor entirely leaves it green.
The bwrap gate is #[cfg(target_os="linux")], so on macOS/Windows the skip is compiled out and the test panics on .expect("tools array") instead of skipping; the import also becomes unused there.

invoke_tool has a SECOND execute_command arm that deserializes flavor with its own default_flavor() and calls tools::execute::execute_command with no enum check. Shadowed today only because jsonrpc_handler intercepts the name earlier, so the 'one canonical check' has a residual bypass one refactor away, plus a third copy of the "minimal" default.

SPEC_KEYS is a union across kinds, so a cross-kind OPTIONAL key (flavor on a subagent spec, system on a sandbox_exec spec) is accepted and then silently ignored - the exact failure mode this change claims to remove - and TEST-5 locks that behaviour in by asserting all five keys succeed together.

resolve_spec_flavor and resolve_execute_flavor are near-identical duplicates (only the arg name and example differ); only the PREDICATE was shared. The default value exists three times (DEFAULT_SANDBOX_FLAVOR, DEFAULT_EXECUTE_FLAVOR, invoke_tool's literal).

spawn_subagent/spawn_sandbox_exec take a &'static KindContract used only for refusals while hardcoding their own JobKind; passing the wrong contract compiles and yields a subagent run demanding spec.command - the same silent-mismatch class the change removes. No type-level link, no test.

read_kind trims but does not reject empty, so {"kind":"subagent","spec":{"kind":"  "}} is refused as BACKGROUND_KIND_CONFLICT with an empty second value printed. An empty string is not a competing kind; the diagnosis is wrong and the input previously succeeded.

missing_spec_field's cross-kind hint uses spec.get(field).is_some(), true for explicit null or a wrong type, so a spec with task:null and command:null is steered toward a kind whose required field is also null. Presence must match what require_spec_field accepts.

The absent/null arm returns the hardcoded default WITHOUT running the allow-list, and nothing asserts is_known_flavor(DEFAULT). A catalog rename would silently make the most-travelled path (no flavor supplied) construct an unknown-flavor download URL - reintroducing the defect.

BACKGROUND_SPEC_REQUIRED says `spec` was not supplied but attaches a SPEC-level example; a model copying it verbatim as its arguments still has no `spec` key. Every sibling refusal attaches a full arguments object.
TEST-17 derives its expected value from the body of the function under test (known_flavor_names), so it cannot fail for any edit to that function. Tautology.

The test-local assert_actionable claims to assert 'the same way' as common::tool_args::conformance::assert_actionable but is weaker: the shared one requires the site's ACTUAL example string, this one only requires the literal "Example: {". A refusal carrying the wrong example passes.

No test round-trips KIND_CONTRACTS[*].example or SANDBOX_FLAVOR_EXAMPLE back through the parser. TEST-5 pins only BACKGROUND_SPEC_EXAMPLE, yet a broken example is exactly the "label" defect this change fixed one level down.

The doc claims everything is table-driven off KIND_CONTRACTS, but nothing pins the schema's kind enums (top-level or nested) against the table, so a third kind would be enforced by the server and never advertised - the advertisement-vs-enforcement gap this change exists to close.

truncate_for_message + MAX_ECHOED_VALUE_CHARS are new public API with zero tests; every test input takes the early-return path, so the documented mid-codepoint panic hazard and the bound itself are unverified.
The echoed fragment is length-bounded but not content-sanitised: backticks/newlines/control chars in a model-supplied kind, key name or flavor pass into the refusal text the model reads next.
The 'no workflow_runs row was created' assertion has no positive control: run_count is only ever observed as unchanged from 0, so a broken run_count (wrong table/DB) would pass while proving nothing.
run_count opens a fresh PgPool per call and never closes it, against the repo's own harness convention (pool.close().await), leaking connections on the shared cluster under parallel test threads.

Untested input classes the parser handles: a NESTED non-string kind (read_kind's whole `location` argument is never asserted), a whitespace-padded kind, a JSON-encoded spec string that also carries a nested kind (the stated reason decode runs first), and more than MAX_REPORTED_UNKNOWN_KEYS unknown keys.

The new INVALID_FLAVOR assertion serializes the whole error body and substring-matches, so it also passes if the token appears in a message field rather than the error-code field the comment claims it pins.
The unreachable `other =>` dispatch arm re-formats a third hand-maintained copy of the BACKGROUND_KIND_UNKNOWN text; the copies can drift with nothing red.

The comment claims the refusal is 'strictly upstream of all of it', but the check sits after build_context, so an invalid-flavor call still pays workspace staging. The ORDERING is deliberate (DEC-12); the CLAIM is what is wrong.

validate_known_flavor's doc claims the admin escape hatch is preserved, but an admin-installed out-of-catalog flavor is now unusable from both tool entry points - the hatch survives for INSTALL, not for USE. The doc overclaims.

The unknown-spec-key refusal turns previously-succeeding calls into failures, and the likeliest offending key is `label` - which this module's own example advertised. Proposes a grace period for previously-ignored keys.
resolution: REJECTED. `label` was never implemented, so a call carrying it was ALREADY silently dropping that field - the model's intent was already not being honoured. A grace period that keeps ignoring previously-ignored keys preserves precisely the silent-ignore this change exists to remove, and would make the new additionalProperties:false advertisement false again. The refusal is actionable (it names the key and lists what is accepted), so a model can fix the call in one turn. The stale-example vector is closed by correcting BACKGROUND_SPEC_EXAMPLE, which this change does.
